summary: ArrowType's site for Recursive Sans & Mono, a free five-axis variable font (MONO, CASL, wght, slnt, CRSV) for code and UI. A three.js hero arranges the letters of 'recursive' through a 3D designspace; a sticky global toolbar (66 named instances, size and every axis) restyles all page prose, which is itself editable markdown in CodeMirror editors with line numbers. Each chapter pairs that prose with an iframe micro-demo (CSS-variable slider sandbox, UI mockups, mono/sans cell widths, robust-layout hover, casual slider, weight pad, slant/cursive slider, named-instance matrix, language list and glyph grid), ending in a free download.

instances.look: On black, the letters r-e-c-u-r-s-i-v-e as nine columns of repeated glyphs in white and greys, each copy an instance at a different weight, casualness and slant, floating in a WebGL scene with thin red (Weight), green (Casual) and blue (Slant) axis lines; the tagline 'A typographic palette for vibrant code & UI' sits under a dotted rule at the bottom
instances.ux: Letters fade in at load (black frame for ~1s); the three.js canvas takes pointer events, probably to orbit the designspace; the fixed nav's 'Get Recursive' button is the CTA
instances.learn: Spell the name through the designspace itself: every repetition of a letter is one coordinate, so the hero is a 3D map of the variable font

instances.learn: One sticky toolbar that drives all the page's body copy lets visitors read the whole story in the style they are evaluating
